## TL;DR

Curl installs now unpack into `~/.local/share/repoos` and leave machine state in `~/.repoos`. Reinstall no longer deletes that state. `repoos uninstall` removes the install, the launcher it owns, and the known state entries, and it names anything it left behind. The installer rejects Node older than 20.6.0. mise is dropped from the recommended install methods. Homebrew still depends on Node because the published bin shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env node`; that evaluation is in `docs/install-layout.md`. Docs and the installer agree on `| bash`.

## Work and rationale

QA on a clean Debian install showed six related failures. They are one layout bug plus copy that described a different product than the installer actually ships.

The layout bug is that `~/.repoos` was both the curl install directory and the machine registry. `install.sh` ran `rm -rf` on it before extracting the tarball, so a reinstall deleted `servers/`, `services.json`, check-slot locks, and agent temp dirs. `repoos uninstall` deleted the same tree and then printed that user configuration was unchanged. Package-manager uninstalls never touched the directory, so `~/.repoos/servers` survived with no message saying so.

The split keeps state where every existing caller already looks: `serversRegistryDir`, the service registry, `localCheckLockRoot`, and `agentRunTmpRoot` all join `homedir()` with `.repoos`. Moving those would be a second migration and would break a running server that still writes the old path. Only the tarball moved. The default install directory is `~/.local/share/repoos` (`REPOOS_INSTALL_DIR` still overrides it). On reinstall, if `~/.repoos/cli/index.js` exists, the script deletes only the payload names shipped in `repoos-dist.tar.gz` (`cli`, `commands`, `core`, `server`, `ui`, `.build-info.json`) and leaves every other entry. If someone points `REPOOS_INSTALL_DIR` back at `~/.repoos`, the same payload-only delete runs instead of removing the directory.

`repoos uninstall` recognizes both the new directory and a legacy combined `~/.repoos` install. A legacy install deletes payload names rather than the whole directory, then deletes the known state entries. Other names under `~/.repoos` are printed and kept. The closing line says per-repo files (`repoos.toml` and each repo's `.repoos/`) were not removed, which is the statement the old message was trying to make and did not. A package-manager install is still not deleted. The command prints npm, Bun, pnpm, and Homebrew uninstall lines, lists the state files still on disk, and tells a mise user to run `mise unuse --global` and `mise prune`. Detection uses the existing `packageManagerUpgrade` path check so Homebrew Cellar and mise install prefixes are covered, not only `node_modules`.

mise is dropped from the published command list (`INSTALL_COMMANDS`, the landing tabs, getting-started, the skill, the starter prompt, and the README). Documenting the flag and the release-age delay would still leave a method that does not install the current release as written, which is the desired UX for every documented method. The caveats stay in `docs/install-layout.md` and in a short getting-started note so an existing mise install is removable. `repoos upgrade` still recognizes a mise path and prints `mise upgrade`.

The Node check is the one-line `node -e` predicate in `install.sh`: major greater than 20, or major 20 and minor greater than 6, or minor exactly 6. That matches `package.json` `engines` of `>=20.6.0`. The old check compared only the major, so 20.0 through 20.5 passed and then failed later. Public copy that said "zero runtime dependencies" or "Node 20+" next to install instructions now says Bun, or Node.js 20.6.0 or newer, and that the package has no runtime npm dependencies. The zero-runtime-dependency rule for this repository's own code is unchanged.

Bun and pnpm PATH friction is documented beside those install commands. Bun's binary lands in `~/.bun/bin`. pnpm on a clean account has no global bin dir, and `pnpm setup` returns `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL` unless `SHELL` is set. The skill repeats both notes so an agent does not paste the bare global install.

Homebrew's Node dependency was evaluated and kept. The curl launcher is bash and prefers Bun. The npm bin is `dist/cli/index.js` with a Node shebang, and Homebrew installs that bin. Removing `depends_on "node"` in `repo-os/homebrew-tap` without shipping the bash launcher would break `brew install` on a Bun-only machine. The formula is not in this repo, so the decision is recorded in `docs/install-layout.md` rather than edited in a tap we do not have checked out.

The installer header now says to pipe to bash, matching the docs. The script still enables `pipefail` only when the shell supports it, but the documented invocation is bash.

## Approaches tried

Moving state to `~/.local/state/repoos` and migrating on startup was the other layout. It would have made "uninstall leaves nothing" a single `rm` of a new directory, but every reader of `~/.repoos/servers` (the server registry, `repoos servers`, the Hub, docs) would need a fallback, and a server already running from the old build would keep writing the old path during the upgrade. Keeping state put and moving only the tarball is the smaller migration: old installs keep working until the next curl install, and that install strips the payload without touching state.

Keeping mise on the list with `allow_low_downloads` and a warning about release age was the other product choice. QA showed that combination still installs the previous version, so a documented command would still fail the "current release as written" bar. Dropping it, and saying so in the docs, matches the acceptance criterion's second option.

## Challenges and blockers

The Homebrew formula is in `repo-os/homebrew-tap`, not this worktree. This change cannot delete the Node dependency. The written evaluation is the deliverable for that criterion.

`compareInstallCommands` treats any fenced line that looks like an install command as published. The mise warning is prose, not a fenced command, so the landing and docs builds stay aligned with the five-command list.

A test that asserted the installer source did not contain `rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"` matched the comment that quoted that exact command. The comment was reworded. Another assertion that InstallBox must not contain the letters `mise` matched the substring inside `Promise`.

## Key learnings

`~/.repoos` in this codebase means two different trees: per-repo cache (`<repo>/.repoos`) and machine state (`~/ .repoos`). Only the second one collided with the curl install. Per-repo data was never what uninstall deleted; the message was wrong because it called machine state "user configuration" and then removed it.

The Node floor was already declared in `engines`. The installer had drifted to a weaker check, and the marketing lines had drifted further to "20+" and "zero dependencies." The engines field is the number the installer and the site should repeat.
